title: Can a knot match its mirror?
hook: Hold a rope trefoil up to a mirror. Can you ever make the rope match its reflection?

knows: what a mirror image is, and that a trefoil is a closed loop with three crossings
doesNotKnow: that turning a knot over is a way of moving it, so it never changes the knot, while its mirror image can be a different knot: no wiggling turns the left-handed trefoil into the right-handed one. The figure-eight is its own mirror image.

misconception: A mirror image is the same knot; you just flip it over.
objective: The learner can explain that turning the trefoil over leaves every crossing mark the same, so it is the same knot, while the mirror changes every mark, and that the trefoil cannot be moved into its mirror image.
keyState: Two milestones on the trefoil: 'turned' (card turned over, unmirrored, marks −,−,−, Sum −3) and 'mirrored' (mirrored on either face, marks +,+,+, Sum +3); each writes its segment of the seen line 'Trefoil: turned over −3 · mirror +3', which is never cleared. Optional, not on the QA path: 'eightMirror' (figure-eight mirrored, Sum 0).

claims.text: The trefoil is chiral: the left- and right-handed trefoils cannot be moved into each other; Max Dehn proved it in 1914 ('Mirroring turned every mark plus, and no wiggling gets back: the trefoil is not its own mirror image, as Max Dehn proved in 1914'; 'So a trefoil comes in a left and a right version'; predict answer 'No, never').
claims.source: Dehn, M. (1914), 'Die beiden Kleeblattschlingen', Math. Ann. 75, 402-413; Wikipedia 'Chiral knot' (research note company/research/notes/2026-10-13-teachable-knot-theory.md §2.4, high; full text unchecked). Brief claim 1 (company/domains/briefs/math.discrete.md, Knots batch 1 #4). Cut first if held: 'as Max Dehn proved in 1914'. Builder-written; unverified.
claims.note: Lane left-or-right W-1605 (fact-checker, 2026-10-17, did not write this claim; base d5235af7): VERIFIED. Rendered text checked in Demo.tsx (reveal paragraph 1, closing sentence, predict key 'No, never'). Own, kit-free: Kauffman bracket on the 3_1 PD gives V = -t^-4 + t^-3 + t^-1, on its mirror V = t + t^3 - t^4; different, so no deformation joins them. Opened: PMC5582600 (Fielden, Leigh, Woltering, Molecular Knots, Angew 2017) section 2.4: 'The trefoil knot 3 1 is topologically chiral, as one mirror-image form cannot be continuously deformed into the other ... the topological chirality of a trefoil knot was only proven mathematically in the early 20th century [30]', ref 30 = M. Dehn, Math. Ann. 1914, 75, 402-413; PMC9948535 (ACS Macro Lett 2023) cites Dehn, Die beiden Kleeblattschlingen, Math. Ann. 1914 for 'cannot be continuously transformed into its mirror image'; Crossref 10.1007/BF01563732 gives title, vol 75, pp 402-413, issued 1914-09. Dehn's own text not opened (Springer host). Non-blocking: the source field still names unopened Wikipedia; builder may swap to PMC5582600 + PMC9948535. Record: company/reviews/left-or-right/2026-10-17-fact-check.md; own script company/reviews/left-or-right/fc-2026-10-17/own.py.

Opened: PMC8199745 (DNA-Topology Simplification by Topoisomerases, 2021): 'An amphichiral knot is, by definition, topologically equivalent to its mirror image ... claims.text: Convention: a crossing mark is plus (right-handed) when the over-strand passes from right to left as seen travelling along the under-strand; a drawing whose marks sum below 0 is called left-handed and above 0 right-handed, and the table's trefoil is the left-handed one (stage 'Left-handed' / 'Right-handed', badges '+' / '−', 'Sum'; reveal 'its hand stayed left'; predict 'A left-handed trefoil and its mirror image, the right-handed one').
claims.source: Library convention, src/lab/knots/README.md 'Conventions' (signs, writhe); sources differ on which trefoil is called right-handed, and the lesson uses the library's. The Sum describes the drawing on show only (reduced alternating, simplify status 'minimal', K1); the stage never calls it an invariant. Brief claim 5. Builder-written; unverified.
claims.note: Lane left-or-right W-1605 (fact-checker, 2026-10-17, did not write this claim; base d5235af7): DISPUTED: the rule sentence is reversed. With the sign the sources use (PMC2853108 Fig. 2E: turn the over-strand's arrow onto the under-strand's, 'If that rotation is clockwise, the crossing is negative and it is positive otherwise'; PMC5582600: 'Positive crossings describe a right-handed helix'), at a plus crossing the over-strand passes from LEFT to RIGHT as seen travelling along the under-strand (under heading north, over heading east); equivalently, travelling along the over-strand, the under-strand passes from right to left. Own check: right-handed double helix X = sin t, Z = cos t, Y = ct gives over SW-to-NE, under SE-to-NW, i.e. left to right seen from the under-strand. The lesson's numbers follow the sources, not this sentence: own signs make the table 3_1 -,-,- and its Jones -t^-4 + t^-3 + t^-1, the left-handed trefoil (PMC2853108: left-handed trefoil writhe about -3.41). So what the learner sees is right ('Left-handed' for the table trefoil, 'plus (right-handed)', sum below 0 called left-handed all check); the claim's convention sentence is wrong as written. Fix for demo-builder (claim text only): 'a crossing mark is plus (right-handed) when the over-strand passes from left to right as seen travelling along the under-strand'. The same reversed sentence is in src/lab/knots/README.md line 37 (Conventions), outside this lane. Record: company/reviews/left-or-right/2026-10-17-fact-check.md; own script company/reviews/left-or-right/fc-2026-10-17/own.py.

claims.text: Turning a knot over in your hands is a way of moving it, so it does not change the knot; the mirror is a reflection, not a move ('turning over is a way of moving it, so its hand stayed left'; 'turning one over never swaps them'; recall answer 'A right-handed trefoil').
claims.source: Definition (a knot is a closed loop up to moving it in space): Adams, The Knot Book (1994), ch. 1 (fact-checker to confirm wording). Brief claim 6. Builder-written; unverified.
claims.note: Lane left-or-right W-1605 (fact-checker, 2026-10-17, did not write this claim; base d5235af7): VERIFIED. Rendered reveal ('turning over is a way of moving it, so its hand stayed left', 'turning one over never swaps them') and recall key 'A right-handed trefoil' checked. Opened: PMC5582600 glossary 'Chiral knot: A knot that cannot be continuously deformed into its mirror image' and section 2.4 (deformation 'without the strand passing through itself'); PMC8199745 (amphichiral = can be continuously deformed into its own mirror image). Own: turning over is rotation by s*pi about an axis in the page, s from 0 to 1, a continuous family of rigid motions, so it is such a deformation; a reflection reverses the orientation of space and lies in no such family. Own computation: turn-over keeps every sign and the Jones polynomial of 3_1; the mirror changes it. Adams not opened; source field swap to PMC5582600 is non-blocking. Record: company/reviews/left-or-right/2026-10-17-fact-check.md; own script company/reviews/left-or-right/fc-2026-10-17/own.py.

recall.question: You hold a right-handed trefoil made of rope. You turn it upside down and lay it flat. What do you have?
options: Either, depending on how you lay it
recall.why: Turning a knot over is a way of moving it, and moving never changes the knot. Only a mirror image swaps the trefoil's hand, and no move reaches it.
